page: Microsoft Azure FX64ms_v2 is a compute- and memory-intensive virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance provides 64 dedicated vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware features include 260 MB of L3 cache, two threads per core, and instruction sets such as AVX-512, Intel AMX (amx_tile, amx_int8), and cryptographic acceleration. It includes 1344.0 GB of system memory, yielding 21.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, without bundled local storage or integrated hardware GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-tier execution across high-throughput and compute workloads. In Geekbench testing, the server attained 2359.0 in single-core and 21986.0 in multi-core metrics, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 85780.36. Large-block memory tests yielded top-decile bandwidth rates of 397.18 GB/s for reads and 172.33 GB/s for writes. The system achieved 37737.47 operations in PassMark database benchmarks, 99.73 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, and 103.39 GB/s in static web serving throughput. CPU-based machine learning inference delivered 3330.57 tokens per second on prompt processing with a 135M model and 36.1 tokens per second on a 70B model.

Because the instance bundles no local disk storage, persistent data access relies entirely on external remote storage attachments. The massive memory allocation combined with high-frequency CPU cores positions the server as an efficient deployment target for in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), real-time analytics, and large-scale relational database engines.
description: Microsoft Azure FX64ms_v2 is a high-frequency, memory-intensive virtual machine running on Microsoft Hyper-V. Powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor with x86_64 architecture, the instance features 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores, 260 MB of L3 cache, and Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions. It is provisioned with 1344.0 GB of memory, delivering an extensive 21.0 GB per vCPU ratio, but includes no local storage or onboard GPUs. In synthetic and application benchmarks, the instance yields top-tier multi-core computing metrics, PassMark database scores of 37737.47, and uncached large-block read memory bandwidth reaching 397.18 GB/s. Redis SET performance achieves 99.73 million operations per second. Lacking local disks, the configuration relies on networked storage solutions. The hardware configuration makes this server optimal for memory-bound relational database management systems, large in-memory caching tiers, CPU-driven inference engines, and memory-heavy scientific simulations.
